akhfash:6-6.t: He said ﴿بِأَيِّكُمُ ٱلْمَفْتُونُ﴾, meaning "أيُّكُمْ المَفْتُون" ("which of you is the afflicted one").

akhfash:51-51.t: And He said ﴿وَإِن يَكَادُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾: this is the "إِنْ" that serves for affirmation. It has the meaning of the heavy (doubled) one, except that it is not heavy; for when you say "إنْ كانَ عبدُ اللهِ لَظَرِيفاً" ("ʿAbdullāh was indeed witty"), its meaning is "إِنْ عبدُ اللهِ لَظَريفٌ قبلَ اليَوْم" ("ʿAbdullāh is indeed witty, before today"). So "إِنْ" enters with this meaning while being light.

daas-irab:43-43.t: ﴿خاشِعَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَبْصارُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil (agent) of خاشعة. ﴿تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ﴾ an imperfect verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and a postponed fāʿil; the clause is a second ḥāl. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw of ḥāl. ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿يُدْعَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿إِلَى السُّجُودِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كانوا, and the clause «قد كانوا..» is a ḥāl clause. ﴿وَهُمْ سالِمُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:44-44.t: ﴿فَذَرْنِي﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the meaning of ذرني is «leave Me»; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the yāʾ of the first person. ﴿يُكَذِّبُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِهذَا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْحَدِيثِ﴾ badal (substitute) of the demonstrative. ﴿سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ﴾ the sīn of futurity, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ حَيْثُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:45-45.t: ﴿وَأُمْلِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); its meaning is «I grant them respite». ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to سنستدرجهم. ﴿إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its predicate; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:46-46.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿تَسْئَلُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَجْراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنْ مَغْرَمٍ مُثْقَلُونَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿مُثْقَلُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:47-47.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿عِنْدَهُمُ﴾ an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿الْغَيْبُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:48-48.t: ﴿فَاصْبِرْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لِحُكْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلا تَكُنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and its noun is latent. ﴿كَصاحِبِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of تكن. ﴿الْحُوتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; he is Yūnus (Jonah), peace be upon him; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being «remember» (اذكر). ﴿نادى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:49-49.t: ﴿لَوْلا﴾ a conditional particle that does not make jussive. ﴿أَنْ تَدارَكَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿نِعْمَةٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نعمة; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being omitted. ﴿لَنُبِذَ﴾ the lām occurring in the apodosis of the condition, and a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِالْعَراءِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:50-50.t: ﴿فَاجْتَباهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿رَبُّهُ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to something implied. ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ﴾ a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and they stand in the place of the second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:51-51.t: ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿إِنْ﴾ lightened (mukhaffafa) and inoperative (muhmala). ﴿يَكادُ الَّذِينَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb and its noun. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾ the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil and the kāf its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِأَبْصارِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the meaning of يزلقونك is: they look at you with such an intense look that it almost throws you down; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of يكاد, and the clause «إن يكاد..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَمَّا﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya). ﴿سَمِعُوا الذِّكْرَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir) [Translator's note: so in the source; the wāw of the plural is ordinarily parsed as the fāʿil]; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَمَجْنُونٌ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿مجنون﴾ its khabar; the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:52-52.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is of ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ذِكْرٌ﴾ khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, an adjective (ṣifa) of ذكر; the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿ن﴾ a letter that has no i'rab; ﴿وَالْقَلَمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of oath, its implied form being «أقسم» (I swear); ﴿وَما﴾ a relative noun, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; ﴿يَسْطُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿ما﴾ operating like «ليس»; ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ its noun; ﴿بِنِعْمَةِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مجنون»; ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of «ما», genitive (majrūr) in form by the redundant (zāʾida) bāʾ, accusative (manṣūb) in position, and the nominal clause is the answer to the oath, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and «إنّ» is a particle resembling the verb; ﴿لَكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar (predicate), and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿أجرا﴾ the delayed noun of «إنّ»; ﴿غَيْرَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «أجرا»; ﴿مَمْنُونٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَإِنَّكَ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿لَعَلى﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿على خُلُقٍ﴾ its khabar (predicate); ﴿عَظِيمٍ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿فَسَتُبْصِرُ﴾ the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَيُبْصِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿بِأَيِّكُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿الْمَفْتُونُ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of one of the two preceding verbs.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿هُوَ أَعْلَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of «إنّ»; ﴿بِمَنْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أعلم»; ﴿ضَلَّ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾ both are attached to «أعلم», and the clause «إن ربك..» gives the reason (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿فَلا تُطِعِ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لا», its fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿الْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿وَدُّوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿لَوْ تُدْهِنُ﴾ «لو» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir) — the meaning of «تدهن» is «تلين لهم» (you would be soft with them) — and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «لو» and the verb is the object of «ودوا», and the clause gives the reason for the prohibition, with no grammatical position; ﴿فَيُدْهِنُونَ﴾ the fāʾ is conjunctive, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:10-13.t: ﴿وَلا تُطِعْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive «لا», whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿كُلَّ﴾ its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿حَلَّافٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿مَهِينٍ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted [noun], and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿هَمَّازٍ، مَشَّاءٍ﴾ two naʿts of the omitted [noun]; ﴿بِنَمِيمٍ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مشاء»; ﴿مَنَّاعٍ﴾ another naʿt; ﴿لِلْخَيْرِ﴾ both are attached to «مناع»; ﴿مُعْتَدٍ، أَثِيمٍ، عُتُلٍّ﴾ naʿts of the same omitted [noun], who is al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq; ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿زَنِيمٍ﴾ another naʿt.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿أَنْ كانَ﴾ «أن» is a maṣdar-forming particle that makes the verb accusative, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); ﴿ذا﴾ its khabar (predicate); ﴿مالٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿وَبَنِينَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «مال».

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive; ﴿تُتْلى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿آياتُنا﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿أَساطِيرُ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿سَنَسِمُهُ﴾ the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿إِنَّا بَلَوْناهُمْ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ», and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿كَما﴾ the kāf is a particle of comparison and a preposition, and «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun); ﴿بَلَوْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿أَصْحابَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ its mafʿūl bihi, annexed to «الجنة»; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «ما» and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by the kāf, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar; ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿أَقْسَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of a genitive by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿لَيَصْرِمُنَّها﴾ the lām falls in the answer to the oath, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of like letters, the dropped wāw being the fāʿil and the «ها» the mafʿūl bihi; ﴿مُصْبِحِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is the answer to the oath, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-18.t: «[Translator's note: the Quranic words of this verse, «وَلا يَسْتَثْنُونَ», are not quoted in the source; the analysis below refers to them.]» «لا» is negating, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿فَطافَ﴾ a past verb; ﴿عَلَيْها﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿طائِفٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent); ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ both are attached to «طائف», and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَهُمْ نائِمُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿فَأَصْبَحَتْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); ﴿كَالصَّرِيمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar (predicate) of «أصبحت», and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿فَتَنادَوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿مُصْبِحِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is conjoined to «أقسموا».

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿أَنِ اغْدُوا﴾ «أن» is an explicative particle (ḥarf tafsīr), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is explicative (mufassira), with no grammatical position; ﴿عَلى حَرْثِكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾ «إن» is conditional and makes the verb jussive, and «كان» and its noun; ﴿صارِمِينَ﴾ its khabar (predicate), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿فَانْطَلَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, [and] a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَتَخافَتُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿أَنْ﴾ explicative (mufassira); ﴿لا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا﴾ «لا» is negating, and an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, the «ها» being the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿مِسْكِينٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent), and the clause is explicative, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿وَغَدَوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿عَلى حَرْدٍ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and «حرد» means withholding from the poor; ﴿قادِرِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿لما﴾ an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive; ﴿رَأَوْها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; ﴿إِنَّا﴾ «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿لَضَالُّونَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿ضالون﴾ its khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb); ﴿نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿قالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿أَلَمْ أَقُلْ﴾ the hamza is interrogative, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لم», its fāʿil being latent (mustatir); ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿لَوْلا﴾ a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); ﴿تُسَبِّحُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:29-29.t: ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿سُبْحانَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; ﴿رَبِّنا﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا﴾ «إنّ» and its noun, and «كان» and its noun; ﴿ظالِمِينَ﴾ its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of «إنّ», and the clause «إنا..» gives the reason (taʿlīl), and the statement «سبحان..» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:30-30.t: ﴿فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿يَتَلاوَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:31-31.t: ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿يا﴾ a vocative particle; ﴿وَيْلَنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf), and the vocative clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿إِنَّا﴾ «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿كُنَّا طاغِينَ﴾ «كان», its noun and its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of «إنّ».

daas-irab:32-32.t: ﴿عَسى رَبُّنا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun; ﴿أَنْ يُبْدِلَنا﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», and its first object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿خَيْراً﴾ its second object, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is the khabar (predicate) of «عسى»; ﴿مِنْها﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خيرا»; ﴿إِنَّا﴾ «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿إِلى رَبِّنا﴾ both are attached to «راغبون»; ﴿راغِبُونَ﴾ the khabar of «إنّ», and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl), and the clause «عسى..» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:33-33.t: ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿الْعَذابُ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَلَعَذابُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); ﴿عذاب الْآخِرَةِ﴾ mubtadaʾ, annexed to «الآخرة»; ﴿أَكْبَرُ﴾ khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿لَوْ﴾ conditional, not making the verb jussive; ﴿كانُوا﴾ «كان» and its noun; ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the khabar of «كانوا», and the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted.

daas-irab:34-34.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb; ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of «إنّ»; ﴿عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ an adverb of place annexed to «ربهم»; ﴿جَنَّاتِ﴾ the delayed noun of «إنّ»; ﴿النَّعِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct).

daas-irab:35-35.t: ﴿أَفَنَجْعَلُ﴾ the hamza is interrogative, the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿كَالْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun in the place of the second object, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:36-36.t: ﴿ما﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause is interrogative, with no grammatical position; ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun, ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿تَحْكُمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:37-37.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction of digression (iḍrāb); ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿كِتابٌ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿فِيهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تدرسون»; ﴿تَدْرُسُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:38-38.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of «إنّ»; ﴿فِيهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb after them; ﴿لَما﴾ the lām is the lām of emphasis; ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, the delayed noun of «إنّ»; ﴿تَخَيَّرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما», and the clause «إنّ..» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «تدرسون».

daas-irab:39-39.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿لَكُمْ أَيْمانٌ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate) and a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «أيمان»; ﴿بالِغَةٌ﴾ a second naʿt; ﴿إِلى يَوْمِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بالغة»; ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to an omitted fronted khabar of «إنّ»; ﴿لَما﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿ما﴾ relative, the delayed noun of «إنّ»; ﴿تَحْكُمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the nominal clause is the answer to an oath implied by «أيمان», with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:40-40.t: ﴿سَلْهُمْ﴾ an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿أَيُّهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿بِذلِكَ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); ﴿زَعِيمٌ﴾ khabar, nominative (marfūʿ), and the nominal clause stands in place of the second object of the verb «سل».

daas-irab:41-41.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿لَهُمْ شُرَكاءُ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate) and a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَلْيَأْتُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿بِشُرَكائِهِمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle making the verb jussive; ﴿كانُوا صادِقِينَ﴾ «كان», its noun and its khabar, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted.

daas-irab:42-42.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ﴾ an adverb of time, and a passive imperfect verb; ﴿عَنْ ساقٍ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and they stand in for the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿وَيُدْعَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil; ﴿إِلَى السُّجُودِ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَلا﴾ «لا» is negating, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it «[Translator's note: the verb meant, «يَسْتَطِيعُونَ», is not quoted in the source.]».

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿نۤ وَٱلْقَلَمِ﴾.
You may conceal the final nūn or make it distinct; making it distinct is preferable to me, because it is a letter-name, and a letter-name is like something paused on even when joined. Whoever conceals it builds on the joining. The readers have read it both ways: al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza used to make it distinct, and some of them leave out the distinctness.

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلاَّفٍ مَّهِينٍ﴾. المهين here is the profligate. And الهماز is the one who slanders people.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿مَّشَّآءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ﴾: نميم and نميمة (tale-bearing) are both of the speech of the Arabs.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿عُتُلٍّ﴾.
In this place it is the one who is fierce in quarrelling falsely. And الزنيم is the one attached to a people who is not of them, namely: the one falsely claimed [as a son] (al-daʿiyy).

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿أَن كَانَ ذَا مَالٍ وَبَنِينَ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read it as a question: "أ أن كان", and some [read] "أن كان" with a single alif, without the question. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ولا تُطِعْ كلَّ حَلاّفٍ مَهِينٍ أن كان: do not obey him because he is (lit. لأِنْ كان) possessed of wealth.
Whoever reads: أ أن كان ذا مال وبنين is rebuking him: Is it because he is possessed of wealth and sons that you obey him? Or if you wish, you may say: Is it because he is possessed of wealth and sons that, when Our verses are recited to him, he says: Tales of the ancients? Both are good.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى ٱلْخُرْطُومِ﴾.
That is: We will brand him with the brand of the people of the Fire, i.e. We will blacken his face. Even though the snout (al-khurṭūm) has been singled out for the brand, it is in the sense of the face, because part of the face stands for the rest.
The Arabs say: أما والله لأسمنّك وسماً لا يفارقك (by Allah, I will brand you with a brand that will not leave you), meaning the nose. One of them recited to me:
لأعْلِطَنَّكَ وسْماً لا يفارقه * كما يُحَزّ بِحُمىَّ المِيسمِ البَحرُ
(I will surely mark you with a brand that will not leave it, as the camel with baḥar is scored with the heat of the branding iron.)
He said "the branding iron" and did not mention the nose, because it is the place of the brand. البحر is a camel afflicted with al-baḥar, a disease that seizes camels, for which they are branded.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿بَلَوْنَاهُمْ﴾.
We tested the people of Mecca as We tested the owners of the garden. They were people of Yemen; one of their men had crops, date palms and vines, and he used to leave for the poor whatever of his crops the sickle missed, whatever of the palms fell onto the spread mats, and whatever of the vines the pickers missed. That used to amount to a great deal, and orphans, widows and the poor lived on it. Then the man died, leaving three sons. They said: Our father used to do that when the wealth was plentiful and the dependants few; but now that the dependants are many and the wealth is little, we will give that up. Then they conspired to harvest in the sadaf — the darkness — remaining of the night, so that nothing would be left for the poor. So Allah set a fire upon their property and burned it. They went early to their property to harvest it and saw nothing but blackness, and said: "إنا لضالُّون" (we have lost our way) — this is not our property. Then one of them said: Rather, it is our property; we have been deprived of it because of what we did to the widows and the poor. They had sworn that they would harvest it at the start of the morning, and they made no exception (lam yastathnū): they did not say "if Allah wills". So a brother of theirs, the most moderate of them, the most just of them in speech, said: Did I not say to you: why do you not glorify [Allah]? Glorifying (tasbīḥ) here has the meaning of making the exception, and it is like His saying: ﴿واذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ إِذَا نَسِيتَ﴾.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَآئِفٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾.
الطائف (a night visitant) is only by night, never by day. The Arabs have used it, saying: أطفت به نهاراً (I visited it by day), though its place is not in the daytime; but it is like your saying: لو ترك القطا ليلا لنام (if the sandgrouse were left alone at night it would sleep), because the sandgrouse does not travel by night. He said: Abū al-Jarrāḥ al-ʿUqaylī recited to me:
أطفت بها نهاراً غير ليلٍ * وألهى ربَّها طلبُ الرّخال
(I came upon it by day, not by night, while its owner was distracted by seeking the ewe-lambs.)
And الرَّخِل is the young of sheep when female.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَٱلصَّرِيمِ﴾: like the blackened night.

farraa:23-24.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱنطَلَقُواْ وَهُمْ يَتَخَافَتُونَ﴾ ﴿أَن لاَّ يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "لا يدخلنها", without أن, because whispering is speech, and speech is quoted; so when [the verb of] saying is not overt, both أن and its omission are permissible, as Allah said: ﴿يُوصِيكُمُ اللهُ فِى أَوْلاَدِكُمْ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الأُنْثَيَيْن﴾ and did not say: أنّ للذّكر; had it been so, it would have been correct.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿وَغَدَوْاْ عَلَىٰ حَرْدٍ قَادِرِينَ﴾.
[I.e.] with earnestness and with power in themselves [203/b]. الحرد also means purpose/direction, as a man says to another: قد أقبلت قِبلك، وقصدت قصدك، وحَرَدْتُ حَردك (I have come your way, made for your direction, headed your heading). One of them recited to me:
وجاء سيلٌ كان من أمر الله * يحرِد حَرْدَ الجنة المُغِلَّهْ
(And a flood came that was of Allah's command, heading straight for the fruitful garden.)
He means: making for it.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّ لَكَ لأَجْراً غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ﴾.
[ممنون means] cut off. The Arabs say: ضعُفت مُنتى عن السفر (my strength has become too weak for travel), and a weak person is called المنين; and this is from that. And Allah knows best.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَلاَوَمُونَ﴾.
Some of them say to others: You are the one who led us and advised us to do what we did. And another says: No, you did that. That is their blaming one another.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ لَكُمْ أَيْمَانٌ عَلَيْنَا بَالِغَةٌ﴾.
The readers read "بالغة" in the nominative, except al-Ḥasan, who read it in the accusative in the manner of a maṣdar (verbal noun), like your saying: حقاً (truly). البالغ is in the sense of "true": it is said جيِّد بالغ (thoroughly good), as if he said: truly good, having reached the reality of goodness. This is a good way. But what the general body [of readers] read — that البالغة is an adjective (naʿt) of الأيمان — is preferable to me, as in your saying: [do you have] oaths binding on Us that will reach with you to the Day of Resurrection, that you shall have whatever you judge? Since the lām is in the answer of إنّ, you give [إنّ] kasra. It is also said: أئن لكم ما تحكمون, as a question, and it has that same meaning, like His saying: ﴿أئذا كُنا تراباً﴾ ﴿أئنا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِى الْحافِرَة﴾.

farraa:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾, that is: a great religion.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿سَلْهُمْ أَيُّهُم بِذَلِكَ زَعِيمٌ﴾.
He means: a guarantor (kafīl). He is also called الحميل, القبيل and الصبير. And الزعيم in the speech of the Arabs is the guarantor, the one who speaks for them, and the one who manages their affairs.
[Translator's note: «القائم يأمرهم» is as printed, presumably for «القائم بأمرهم» ("the one who manages their affairs").]

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكَآءُ فَلْيَأتُواْ بِشُرَكَآئِهِمْ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "أم لهم شرك فليأتوا بشركهم". شِرك and شركاء have one meaning: you say: فى هذا الأمر شِرْك (in this matter there are partners) and فيه شركاء.

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَن سَاقٍ﴾.
The readers are agreed on ḍamma on the yāʾ. [Muḥammad told us,] he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Sufyān told me, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read: "يوم تكشف عن ساق", meaning the Resurrection and the Hour, because of its severity. He said: and one of the Arabs recited to me, by the grandfather of Abū Ṭarafa:
كشفَتْ لهم عن ساقها * وبدا من الشرِّ البراحُ
(It [war] bared its shin to them, and the evil became plainly manifest.)

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿فَذَرْنِي وَمَن يُكَذِّبُ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ﴾.
The meaning of "leave Me and whoever denies" is: entrust them to Me. You say to a man: لو تركتك ورأيك ما أفلحت (had I left you to your own judgement, you would not have prospered), i.e.: had I entrusted you to your judgement, you would not have prospered. Likewise His saying: ﴿ذَرْنِى وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ وحِيداً﴾. (من) is in the position of the accusative. When you say: قد تُرِكتَ ورأيَك and خُليت ورأيك (you have been left to your judgement), you put الرأى in the accusative, because the meaning is: you were left to your judgement; so you make the second accusative because this meaning suits it, and because the noun before it is attached to a verb.
But when the Arabs say: لو تركت أنت ورأيُكَ, they make it nominative because of the strength of أنت, since it is overt and not attached to the verb.
Likewise they say: لو ترك عبدالله والأسدُ لأكله (if ʿAbd Allāh and the lion were left together, it would eat him). If they use a pronoun for ʿAbd Allāh and say: لو ترك والأسدَ أكله, they put [الأسد] in the accusative, because the noun is not overt. If they say: لو ترك هو والأسد, they prefer the nominative in الأسد. What is permissible in the one is permissible in the other, except that the speech of [204/a] the Arabs is as I have informed you — except for their saying: قد ترك بعضُ القوم وبعض (some of the people were left with others), where they prefer agreement (itbāʿ), because بعض and بعض, since they agree in meaning and name, agreement was chosen for them; yet the accusative in the second is not ruled out.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ عِندَهُمُ ٱلْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ﴾.
He is saying: Do they have the Preserved Tablet, so that they write from it and dispute with you by it?

farraa:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلْحُوتِ﴾.
[I.e.] like Jonah ﷺ. He is saying: do not become exasperated with them as Jonah became exasperated, so that he fled from his people and cast himself into the sea, until the fish swallowed him.

farraa:49-50.t:
His saying: ﴿لَّوْلاَ أَن تَدَارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ﴾.
[I.e., he would have been cast out] at the time he was cast out while blameworthy; but he was cast out not blameworthy. ﴿فَٱجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "لولا أن تداركته". That is like His saying: ﴿وَأخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ and ﴿وأخذت﴾ in another place, because نعمة is a feminine noun derived from a verb, and when its verb comes first you may make it masculine or feminine.
His saying: ﴿لَنُبِذَ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ﴾. العراء is the [bare] land.
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us, he said: al-Farrāʾ told us.]
[Translator's note: «نبد عير مذموم» is as printed, for «نُبذ غيرَ مذموم».]

farraa:5-6.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَتُبْصِرُ وَيُبْصِرُونَ﴾ ﴿بِأَيِّكُمُ ٱلْمَفْتُونُ﴾.
المفتون here has the meaning of madness (al-junūn): it is in the manner of [the maṣdar] الفتون, as they said: ليس له معقول رأى (he has no sound judgement), [using a passive-participle form as a maṣdar]. And if you wish, you may take بأيكم as فى أيكم, i.e.: in which of the two parties is the madman; it is then a noun, not a maṣdar.

farraa:51-52.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِن يَكَادُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصَارِهِمْ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it: (ليُزلِقونك) with ḍamma on the yāʾ, from أزلقتُ; and the people of Medina read it: (ليَزلقونك) with fatḥa on the yāʾ, from زَلَقْتُ. The Arabs say of one who shaves the head: قد زلقه and أزلقه. Ibn ʿAbbās read it: "ليُزْهقونك بأبصارهم". Muḥammad told us, he said: I heard al-Farrāʾ say: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna told us that, from a man, [from] Ibn ʿAbbās. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd it is likewise with hāʾ: "ليزهقونك", i.e.: they would strike you down with their eyes. That is because when one of the Arabs wanted to put the evil eye on property — i.e. to strike it with the eye — he would starve himself for three days, then confront that property and say: By Allah, [I have never seen] property more abundant or finer [meaning: I have not seen more abundant], and camels would fall down from it. They wanted to do the like with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: We have never seen the like of his arguments; and they looked at him to strike him with the eye, and said: We have never seen the like of him, and he is surely mad. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَمَا هُوَ إِلاَّ ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ﴾. It is also said: (وإن كادوا ليزلقونك), i.e.: they would hurl you from your place and remove you from it with their eyes, as you say: كاد يصرعنى بشدة نظره (he almost felled me with the intensity of his gaze); this is clear and frequent in the speech of the Arabs, as you say: أزهقت السهم فزهق (I sent the arrow flying and it went).
[Translator's note: «عن رجل ابن عباس» is as printed; a «عن» seems to have dropped out before «ابن عباس». The printed text also has «فرهق», translated as «فزهق».]

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿وَدُّواْ لَوْ تُدْهِنُ﴾.
It is said: they wished that you would be pliant in your religion, so that they would be pliant in theirs. And some said: that you would disbelieve, so that they would disbelieve, i.e.: so that they would follow you in disbelief.
[Translator's note: «لو تفكر فيكفرون» is as printed, evidently for «لو تكفر فيكفرون».]

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أنْ كانَ ذا مالٍ وبَنِينَ﴾ ("because he is possessed of wealth and sons"). It has also been read in the form of a question, and the meaning is that of rebuke (tawbīkh). The position of «أنْ» is accusative (naṣb), on two lines: on the meaning "Is it because he is possessed of wealth and sons that he says, when Our verses are recited to him…?", so «أنْ» is accusative, meaning "he said that because he was possessed of wealth and sons"; that is, he made unbelief in Our signs the repayment for the blessing of wealth and sons he had been granted. When the alif of interrogation comes, this is the view, and nothing else is valid. And it was said in the exegesis: "And do not obey every despicable swearer of oaths … because he is possessed of wealth and sons", that is: do not obey him on account of his affluence and his numbers. And «أساطِيرُ» ("tales") is nominative (marfūʿ) by the implied «هِيَ» ("they are"); the meaning is: "When Our verses are recited to him, he says: they are the tales of the ancients." The singular of «الأساطِير» is «أُسْطُورَة».

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿سَنَسِمُهُ عَلى الخُرْطُومِ﴾ ("We shall brand him on the snout"): its meaning is "We shall brand him on his nose"; «الخُرْطُوم» is the nose. The meaning of «سَنَسِمُهُ» is: We shall give him in the Hereafter the mark by which the people of the Fire are known, namely the blackening of their faces. And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that He singles him out with a brand of his own, because of the extremity of his enmity to the Prophet (peace be upon him), so that he is marked out with a disfigurement by which he is distinguished from others, just as his enmity to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was an enmity by which he was distinguished from others.

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿إنّا بَلَوْناهم كَما بَلَوْنا أصْحابَ الجَنَّةِ إذْ أقْسَمُوا لَيَصْرِمُنَّها مُصْبِحِينَ﴾ ("We have tried them as We tried the owners of the garden, when they swore they would surely cut its fruit in the morning"). «الجَنَّة» is the orchard. These were a people in the region of Yemen. They had a father who used to give charity to the poor from his garden. It has come in the exegesis that he used to take from it his provision for the year and give the rest in charity; and it has also come that he used to leave for the poor whatever the sickle missed, whatever was at the bottom of the stacks, whatever the grape-pickers missed, and whatever fell outside the mat spread beneath the palm tree when its fruit was cut, so that a great deal would collect from that. His sons said: "We are many, and if we do with the poor what our father used to do, things will become hard for us." So they swore they would cut its fruit in the darkness before dawn (sudfa). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلا يَسْتَثْنُونَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 18] ("and they made no exception"), i.e. they swore and did not say "If Allah wills." When the time they had appointed came, in the darkness before dawn, they went early to their garden to cut its fruit.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَطافَ عَلَيْها طائِفٌ مِن رَبِّكَ وهم نائِمُونَ﴾ ("Then there came upon it a visitation from your Lord while they slept"), i.e. He sent upon it a punishment from the sky, and it was burnt entirely.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
﴿فَأصْبَحَتْ كالصَّرِيمِ﴾ ("So it became like the cut-off [crop]"), i.e. it became black as the night.
﴿فَتَنادَوْا مُصْبِحِينَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 21] ﴿أنِ اغْدُوا عَلى حَرْثِكم إنْ كُنْتُمْ صارِمِينَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 22] ("And they called to one another in the morning: Go early to your crop if you would cut it"), i.e. if you are resolved upon cutting the dates.

zajjaj:23-23.t: ﴿فانْطَلَقُوا وهم يَتَخافَتُونَ﴾ ("So they set out, whispering to one another"), i.e. speaking secretly among themselves with ﴿أنْ لا يَدْخُلَنَّها اليَوْمَ عَلَيْكم مِسْكِينٌ﴾ [al-Qalam: 24] ("Let no poor person enter it upon you today"). «التَّخافُت» is speaking secretly.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
﴿وَغَدَوْا عَلى حَرْدٍ قادِرِينَ﴾ ("And they went early, ḥard, [thinking themselves] able"): from their saying «حارَدَتِ السَّنَةُ» ("the year was barren"), when it withholds its bounty. It was also said: "in anger". As for «الحَرْد» meaning purpose/heading towards, they recited concerning it:
؎أقْبَلَ سَيْلٌ جاءَ مِن أمْرِ اللَّهْ ∗∗∗ يَحْرِدُ حَرْدَ الجَنَّةِ المُغِلَّةْ
(A torrent came on, sent by Allah's command, making for the fruitful garden.)
That is: heading straight for the fruitful garden. ﴿فَلَمّا رَأوْها قالُوا إنّا لَضالُّونَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 26] ("But when they saw it, they said: Surely we have lost our way").

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿فَلَمّا رَأوْها﴾ ("But when they saw it") burnt, ﴿قالُوا إنّا لَضالُّونَ﴾ ("they said: Surely we have lost our way"), i.e. we have strayed from the path to our garden; that is: this is not it. Then they knew that it was a punishment, and they said: ﴿بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 27] ("Nay, rather we have been deprived"), i.e. we have been deprived of the fruit of our garden because we withheld it from the poor.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
﴿قالَ أوْسَطُهم ألَمْ أقُلْ لَكم لَوْلا تُسَبِّحُونَ﴾ ("The most moderate of them said: Did I not say to you, why do you not glorify [Allah]?"). «أوْسَطُهُمْ» means the most just of them, from His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْناكم أُمَّةً وسَطًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 143] ("And thus We have made you a middle nation"), i.e. just. ﴿لَوْلا تُسَبِّحُونَ﴾: he said to them: make an exception (istithnāʾ) in your oath — because they had sworn they would cut its fruit in the morning and made no exception. The meaning of tasbīḥ (glorification) here is the exception, that is, saying "If Allah wills." If someone says: "tasbīḥ is saying 'Glory be to Allah (subḥān Allāh)'", the answer to that is that everything by which you magnify Allah is tasbīḥ, because tasbīḥ in the language — according to what has come from the Prophet (peace be upon him) — is declaring Allah free of every evil; and the exception is a magnification of Allah and an acknowledgement that no one is able to do any deed except by His will, Mighty and Majestic.
So the meaning of His saying ﴿إنّا بَلَوْناهم كَما بَلَوْنا أصْحابَ الجَنَّةِ﴾ [al-Qalam: 17] ("We have tried them as We tried the owners of the garden") is: We tried the people of Mecca when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against them, saying: «"O Allah, make Your tread heavy upon Muḍar, and make it upon them years like the years of Joseph"», and Allah tried them with scab, destruction and the loss of provisions, just as He tried the owners of this garden with its burning and the loss of their provision from it.

zajjaj:35-36.t: His saying: ﴿أفَنَجْعَلُ المُسْلِمِينَ كالمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ ﴿ما لَكم كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ﴾ ("Shall We then treat those who submit like the criminals? What is wrong with you? How do you judge?"). This alif is the alif of interrogation, and its sense here is rebuke and making them acknowledge (taqrīr). It has come in the exegesis that one of the unbelievers of Quraysh said: "If what they mention is true, that they have a share in the Hereafter, then we shall have in the Hereafter more than that, just as in this world we are better off than they are." So Allah rebuked them, saying: ﴿أفَنَجْعَلُ المُسْلِمِينَ كالمُجْرِمِينَ﴾, and likewise ﴿ما لَكم كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ﴾, meaning: "On which of the states of unbelief do you base your judgement?!"

zajjaj:37-38.t: ﴿أمْ لَكم كِتابٌ فِيهِ تَدْرُسُونَ﴾ ﴿إنَّ لَكم فِيهِ لَما تَخَيَّرُونَ﴾ ("Or do you have a scripture in which you study, that you shall surely have in it whatever you choose?"), i.e. do you have a scripture from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, stating that you shall have whatever you choose?!

zajjaj:39-39.t: ﴿أمْ لَكم أيْمانٌ عَلَيْنا بالِغَةٌ﴾ ("Or do you have oaths binding on Us, bāligha"): it means "confirmed"; ﴿إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ إنَّ لَكم لَما تَحْكُمُونَ﴾ ("until the Day of Resurrection, that you shall have whatever you judge?"), i.e. a sworn oath upon what you claim in your judgement.

zajjaj:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿سَلْهم أيُّهم بِذَلِكَ زَعِيمٌ﴾ ("Ask them which of them is the guarantor of that"). «الزَّعِيم» is the surety and the guarantor; the meaning is: "Ask them which of them has stood surety for that?!"

zajjaj:41-42.t:
His saying: ﴿أمْ لَهم شُرَكاءُ فَلْيَأْتُوا بِشُرَكائِهِمْ إنْ كانُوا صادِقِينَ﴾ ﴿يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ ساقٍ﴾ ("Or do they have partners? Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful — on the Day when the shin is laid bare"), i.e. let them bring their partners on the Day of Resurrection. The meaning of ﴿يُكْشَفُ عَنْ ساقٍ﴾ in the language is: the grave matter is laid bare. The poet said:
؎قَدْ شَمَّرَتْ عَنْ ساقِها فَشُدُّوا ∗∗∗ وجَدَّتِ الحَرْبُ بِكم فَجِدُّوا
؎والقَوْسُ فِيها وتَرٌ عُرُدُ
(War has bared its shin, so brace yourselves; war has grown earnest with you, so be earnest — and the bow has a tough, taut string.)
And it has come in the exegesis from Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, who said: my father narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar — meaning Ghundar — narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said concerning His saying ﴿يُكْشَفُ عَنْ ساقٍ﴾: "[It is laid bare] from the grave matter." And Ibn Masʿūd said: "The All-Merciful will uncover His shin; as for the believers, they will fall down before Him prostrating, and as for the hypocrites, their backs will become one rigid piece (ṭabaqan ṭabaqan), as though there were skewers in them." This is what we have narrated in the exegesis, and what the lexicographers have said.
[Translator's note: the isnad as printed begins «عَنْ أحْمَدَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أحْمَدَ بْنِ حَنْبَلَ … ثَنا أبِي»; the narrator from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal is normally his son ʿAbd Allāh, so the chain may be garbled in the source. Translated as written.]
Abū Isḥāq said: This is the interpretation of His saying: ﴿وَيُدْعَوْنَ إلى السُّجُودِ فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾ ﴿خاشِعَةً أبْصارُهُمْ﴾ [al-Qalam: 43] ("and they will be called to prostrate, but they will not be able — their eyes downcast"); the hypocrites are meant by it.
And His saying: ﴿تَرْهَقُهم ذِلَّةٌ﴾ [al-Qalam: 43] means: abasement will cover them; ﴿وَقَدْ كانُوا يُدْعَوْنَ إلى السُّجُودِ وهم سالِمُونَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 43] ("and they used to be called to prostrate while they were sound"): what is meant by it is: in this world.

zajjaj:44-44.t: His saying: ﴿فَذَرْنِي ومَن يُكَذِّبُ بِهَذا الحَدِيثِ﴾ ("So leave Me with whoever denies this discourse"); and similar to it is ﴿ذَرْنِي ومَن خَلَقْتُ وحِيدًا﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 11] ("Leave Me with the one I created alone"). Its meaning is: do not occupy your heart with him; leave him to Me, for I shall requite him. Similar to it is a man's saying: "Leave me and him" — it does not mean that he was preventing him from doing so; rather its interpretation is: "Leave him to me, for I shall spare you the trouble of him."

zajjaj:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿فاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ ولا تَكُنْ كَصاحِبِ الحُوتِ﴾ ("So be patient for the judgement of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish"): He means Jonah (peace be upon him).
﴿إذْ نادى وهو مَكْظُومٌ﴾ ("when he called out while he was makẓūm"), i.e. filled with grief and distress.

zajjaj:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوْلا أنْ تَدارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِن رَبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ بِالعَراءِ وهو مَذْمُومٌ﴾ ("Had not a favour from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast onto the barren shore while blameworthy"). The meaning is that he was cast onto the barren shore while not blameworthy; what shows this is that the favour had encompassed him.
And His saying: ﴿فاجْتَباهُ رَبُّهُ﴾ [al-Qalam: 50] ("But his Lord chose him"): this is a clearing of him from blame. «العَراء» is the empty place. The poet said:
؎رَفَعْتُ رِجْلًا لا أخافُ عِثارَها ∗∗∗ ونَبَذْتُ بِالبَلَدِ العَراءِ ثِيابِي
(I lifted a foot whose stumbling I did not fear, and cast off my clothes in the barren land.)

zajjaj:51-51.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإنْ يَكادُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأبْصارِهِمْ﴾ ("And those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes"). It was also read «لَيُزْهِقُونَكَ» with hāʾ, but this — I mean the hāʾ — contradicts the Muṣḥaf, and the reading follows what agrees with the Muṣḥaf. This verse needs a section of explanation from the language. As for what has been narrated in the exegesis: it is narrated that when a man of the Arabs wanted to strike something with the evil eye (yaʿtān), i.e. afflict it with the eye, he would starve himself for three days, then say to what he wanted to strike with the eye: "I have not seen camels — or sheep, or whatever he wanted — like today's!" The meaning is: "I have not seen camels like the camels I see today." By this saying he would afflict them with the eye. So they said to the Prophet ﷺ, when they heard the Reminder from him, what they used to say to whatever they wanted to strike with the eye.
As for the doctrine of the lexicographers, the interpretation according to them is that out of the intensity of their hatred and hostility towards you, they almost harm you with their looking — the look of hatred. This is used in speech; one says: "He looked at me with a look that almost floored me," and "a look with which he almost devoured me." Its interpretation in every case is that he looked at me with a look such that, had he been able along with it to devour me or floor me, he would have done so. This is clear and evident, and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Nūn
Makkan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ن والقَلَمِ وما يَسْطُرُونَ﴾ — it was read with the nūn assimilated into the wāw; it was read with the nūn pronounced distinctly before the wāw; and it was read ”نُونَ والقَلَمِ“ with a fatḥa on the nūn. The one who chose assimilating the nūn into the wāw (did so), whether the wāw [Translator's note: so printed; the nūn is evidently meant] is quiescent or vowelled, because what has come in the exegesis removes it from being quiescent and pronounced distinctly; for whoever makes it quiescent and pronounces it distinctly only treats it as a letter of the alphabet, whereas the one who assimilates it may assimilate it while it carries a fatḥa. [Translator's note: the passage is compressed in the text as transmitted.] It has come in the exegesis that ”نُونْ“ is the whale on which the seven earths were spread out; and it has also come in the exegesis that the nūn is the inkwell. It has not come in the exegesis in the way I interpreted the letters of the alphabet; and quiescence is only permissible if it is a letter of the alphabet. It has come in the exegesis that the first thing Allah created was the Pen, and He said to it: (Write). It said: "O Lord, and what shall I write?" He said: (The decree). So the Pen ran with all that will be until the Day of Resurrection; and among what the Pen ran with was: ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدا أبِي لَهَبٍ﴾ [al-Masad: 1]. His saying: ﴿وَما يَسْطُرُونَ﴾ means: and what the angels write.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿ما أنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾ — this is a question from the chapters of grammar which needs explanation. His saying ”أنْتَ“ is the ism (subject) of ”ما“, and ”بِمَجْنُونٍ“ is the khabar (predicate), and ”بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ“ is connected with the sense of negation. The meaning is: "Madness is negated from you by the favour of your Lord," just as you say "أنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ فَهِمٌ" (by the favour of Allah you are intelligent) and "ما أنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ جاهِلٌ" (by the favour of Allah you are not ignorant), its interpretation being: "ignorance has left you by the favour of your Lord." This is a reply to their saying: ﴿وَقالُوا يا أيُّها الَّذِي نُـزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ إنَّكَ لَمَجْنُونٌ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 6].

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ لَكَ لأجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ﴾ means: not cut off; and it has come in the exegesis: "not counted."

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿وَإنَّكَ لَعَلى خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ — it is said: upon Islam; and it is said: upon the Quran. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "You are upon the character which Allah commanded you in the Quran."

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَتُبْصِرُ ويُبْصِرُونَ﴾ ﴿بِأيِّيكُمُ المَفْتُونُ﴾ [al-Qalam: 6] — the meaning of ”اَلْمَفْتُونُ“ is: the one who has been afflicted with madness. Abū ʿUbayda said: the bāʾ is meant to be discarded; the meaning is "which of you is the afflicted one." He said: and like it is the saying of the poet:
؎نَضْرِبُ بِالسَّيْفِ ونَرْجُو بِالفَرَجِ
(We strike with the sword and hope for relief.)
He said its meaning is "we hope for relief." But it is not so; the meaning is "we hope for the removal of what we are in by relief," or "we hope for victory by relief." The bāʾ in ”بِأيِّكُمُ المَفْتُونُ“ cannot be redundant (laghw); that is not permissible in Arabic in the view of any of its authorities. There are two views on it among the grammarians. They said ”اَلْمَفْتُونُ“ here is in the sense of ”اَلْفُتُونُ“ (affliction): maṣdars (verbal nouns) come on the pattern of the passive participle. The Arabs say "لَيْسَ لِهَذا مَعْقُولٌ", i.e. intelligence (ʿaql), and "لَيْسَ لَهُ مَعْقُودُ رَأْيٍ" in the sense of "firmness of opinion (ʿaqd raʾy)," and you say "دَعْهُ إلى مَيْسُورٍ" in the sense of "to ease (yusr)." So the meaning is: "You will see and they will see in which of you is the affliction." There is another view: "in which of you is the afflicted one" — in the party you are in, or in the party of the disbelievers among whom are Abū Jahl, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī and those like them. On this view the meaning is: "You will see and they will see in which of the two parties the madman is: in the party of Islam or in the party of disbelief."

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ﴾ means: "They wish that you would compromise with them in religion, so that they would compromise with you."

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَلا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلافٍ مَهِينٍ﴾ — (”مَهِينٍ“ is on the pattern) ”فَعِيلٌ“ from ”اَلْمَهانَةُ“, which is paltriness; its meaning here is paltriness of judgement and discernment.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿هَمّازٍ مَشّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ﴾ — ”اَلْهَمّازُ“ is the one who backbites people.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿مَنّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ أثِيمٍ﴾ — its meaning is: he used to hold back his family, his children and his kin from Islam. It has come in the exegesis that he was al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī; he was well-off and of great wealth, and he had ten sons, and he used to say to them and to his kin: "Whoever of you embraces Islam, I will withhold my support from him."

His saying: ﴿مُعْتَدٍ أثِيمٍ﴾ means: exceeding the bounds in wrongdoing. ”أثِيمٍ“ means: sinful towards his Lord, i.e. sinful through his transgression and his offence.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿عُتُلٍّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ زَنِيمٍ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that the ʿutull here is the one fierce in disputing; and it has come in the exegesis that he is the coarse of character, base of nature. In the language it is the rough and coarse one. As for ”اَلزَّنِيمُ“, it has come in the language that he is the one attached to a people while not being one of them. Ḥassān ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī said:
؎وَأنْتَ زَنِيمٌ نِيطَ في آلِ هاشِمٍ ∗∗∗ كَما نِيطَ خَلْفَ الرّاكِبِ القَدَحُ الفَرْدُ
(You are an adventitious hanger-on, attached to the family of Hāshim, as the lone cup is tied on behind the rider.)
And it is said that the zanīm is the one known for evil, as a goat is known by its wattle (zanama); ”اَلزَّنَمَتانِ“ are the two wattles hanging at the throats of goats.
